conviction_note: The negatives are real but mostly priced. Mortgage rates rose from 6.67% in mid-August to 7.40% by mid-October, refi applications fell 56% YoY and existing-home sales were weak; the stock is down about 22% since early August and 14.7% over 20 days, sits 6% above its 52-week low, and short interest is light at 3.7%. So p_up is 46, only slightly below 50, on an abs move of 5.5 (the median reaction of 3.91 raised because a Q4 rate-shock commentary is likely and realised vol is 52%). That gives -0.44, against a findings sum of -1.1. The gap is the sold-down positioning, which the per-finding sizes carry only in the +0.5 positioning item.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.63 and revenue $938.6M per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/STC/earnings-forecasts). A second source, Tickflow (https://tickflow.io/stock/STC/forecast), shows $1.85 / $902M and looks stale. Dowling & Partners cut FY26 EPS to $5.26 from $5.80 on 2026-07-29 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dowling-partn-has-negative-outlook-for-stc-fy2026-earnings-2026-07-29/). With H1 adjusted EPS at $2.17, that implies roughly $1.55-1.60 a quarter for H2. The bar is DISPUTED, so every finding is capped small. Year-ago comparison: Q3 2025 adjusted EPS $1.64 on revenue $796.9M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/94344/000110465925101536/tm2529213d1_ex99-1.htm). No company guidance exists beyond the Q2 call's 'no residential market growth in H2'.
positioning_check: Short interest 1,119,271 shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 3.7% of shares outstanding, 3.20 days to cover, down from a 1,210,463 peak on 2026-09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/stc/shortinterest, read 2026-10-21). Not a crowded short. Skew: none; the baseline chain is unusable (ATM spread 184% of mid, total OI 183, put/call OI 0.18), ATM IV 57.1% for the 30-day expiry. Unusual Whales shows a ±10.36% implied earnings move (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/STC/earnings), but it comes off the same illiquid chain, so it is not used as the scale. Tape: run-up 5d +3.99%, 20d -14.7%, 31.5% below the 52-week high, 6.35% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: The 30-year mortgage rate (Freddie Mac PMMS) went from 6.67% on 2026-08-13 to 6.95% on 09-17, 7.03% on 09-24, 7.28% on 10-01 and 7.40% on 10-08 and 10-15. MBA applications for the week ending 10-02: refinance -8% week on week and -56% YoY, purchase -15% YoY, contract rate 7.49%. October orders and Q4 commentary on tomorrow's 08:30 call will reflect the worst rate backdrop since 2023.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: STC gives no formal guidance; the outlook is commentary on the call. The July 2026 print (revenue beat, EPS miss, management saying no H2 residential growth) fell -7.83%. October 2025 fell -4.1% on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. STC is down about 22% from $68 on 2026-08-05 and 14.7% over 20 days, and FAF fell from about $70 to $62 over the same span. What is not yet priced is how bad October open orders are: management will quantify them on the call, and a refi collapse of this size could still surprise on the downside. If fully priced, the stock would sit at or below its 52-week low; it is 6% above it.
findings.independence: MBA weekly survey via JM Financial, 2026-10-08 (https://www.jmfinancialservices.in/market-news-and-insights/1735637). Tradingeconomics on the October climb (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/30-year-mortgage-rate/news/588887). These are separate series showing the same rate shock.

findings.finding: Q3 residential volume was weak. NAR says August and September were the slowest sales months of 2026; September existing-home sales were 3.99M SAAR, down 2.2% YoY and lower in all four regions. Q3 2025 had a September refi bump at lower rates, so Q3 2026 residential orders are likely down YoY, offset partly by fee per file (+10% to $3,200 in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 domestic non-commercial revenue was -1% YoY, and the stock fell -7.83% on that print, though the cause there was title margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: NAR data is public and management said on the Q2 call it did not expect H2 residential market growth, so this lands inside what the company already guided. Filed small for completeness.
findings.independence: RISMedia, 2026-10-13 (https://www.rismedia.com/2026/10/13/existing-home-sales-up-monthly-down-year-over-year/). This rests on the same NAR release, so it is one fact.

findings.finding: MSCI data cited by CRE Daily on 2026-09-30: US individual commercial property sales fell 28% YoY in August 2026, while entity-level M&A hit a record. STC's domestic commercial title revenue was +20% YoY in Q2 and about +30% in H1, driven by energy and data centres, and is the company's growth engine.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Commercial strength has carried the revenue beats (Q2 revenue beat by about $50M), and the stock still fell on margin.
findings.why_not_priced: Commercial is widely seen as STC's resilient line (management: 'commercial will remain more resilient'), so a single-month industry slowdown in property-level deals is not in the narrative. This is a proxy, though: STC's mix (energy, data centres, large deals, new commercial hires) differs from the MSCI series, and MSCI expects the decline to narrow as small-market deals get reported.
findings.independence: Proxy only. The company's own Q2 number (+20% domestic commercial, closed commercial orders +21%) points the other way: https://s27.q4cdn.com/679580685/files/doc_news/Stewart-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf

findings.finding: In Q2 2026, revenue grew 24.5% but adjusted EPS only 4% ($1.39 vs $1.34), missing consensus by about $0.24. Title segment adjusted pretax margin fell to 6.9% from 8.5% on higher outside search fees and staffing; consolidated other operating expenses rose to 27.4% of revenue from 24.6%; corporate interest expense rose on acquisition debt. The Q3 bar of $1.63 is flat on Q3 2025's $1.64, so a repeat of the margin compression misses again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: revenue beat with EPS miss on margin, -7.83%. October 2025: EPS beat, -4.1%. July 2025: +10.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the July miss triggered downgrades from KBW, Zacks and Wall Street Zen. But Benzinga's Q3 consensus of $1.63 still implies flat YoY EPS on about 18% revenue growth, the same structure Q2 missed. If the bar had absorbed the margin trend it would sit nearer the $1.55 implied by Dowling's $5.26 FY figure. Because the bar is disputed, this finding is capped.
findings.independence: Dowling & Partners FY26 cut to $5.26 from $5.80, 2026-07-29 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/dowling-partn-has-negative-outlook-for-stc-fy2026-earnings-2026-07-29/). KBW downgrade to market perform, target $71, 2026-07-27 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/stewart-information-services-nysestc-downgraded-to-market-perform-rating-by-keefe-bruyette-woods-2026-07-27/).

findings.finding: The stock is sold down into the print: about $52.9 against $68.04 on 2026-08-05 (-22%), 6% above its 52-week low. Short interest is light and falling (3.7% of shares outstanding, 3.2 days to cover, off a 09-15 peak), and the sell-side average target ($81.50) is stale. A merely in-line quarter leaves room for relief.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of 7 prints, 4 were up. The biggest up move, +10.2% in July 2025, came after a stretch near 52-week lows (a 52-week low on 2025-07-15).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition in the price. The point is that the drawdown has a sourced cause (rates) already reflected, so the asymmetry on a not-bad print favours the upside. If the market expected a clean print, the stock would not be within 6% of its low.
findings.independence: Robinhood snapshot showing $68.04 on 2026-08-05 (https://robinhood.com/us/en/stocks/stc/). MarketBeat note on the July 2025 52-week low followed by a +10.2% print reaction (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/stewart-information-services-nysestc-reaches-new-12-month-low-heres-why-2025-07-15).

findings.finding: Revenue is supported inorganically. The MCS acquisition ($330M, announced November 2025) lifted Real Estate Solutions revenue 75% to $197.4M in Q2 at a 13.6% adjusted margin, and gross agency title revenue grew 25%. Q2 revenue beat consensus by about $52M, so a revenue beat against $938.6M is likely again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been rewarded: Q2 2026 revenue beat by about $52M and the stock fell -7.83%.
findings.why_not_priced: A revenue beat is the expected pattern after Q2 and this stock does not trade on revenue, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Benzinga Q2 actual vs estimate, revenue $899.2M vs $847.1M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/STC/earnings-forecasts). This shares the Q2 release with the margin finding: that one is about EPS conversion, this one about the top line, and they are not double-counted.

findings.finding: FHFA Director Pulte said in June 2026 that Fannie Mae is expanding its title-waiver pilot, which lets refinances under 80% LTV skip lender title policies, with more vendors to be added. Analysts may ask about it on the call, and a refi-heavy backdrop makes it less relevant in the near term.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2025 the pilot's expansion knocked title stocks 7-8% intraday (FAF -8%, FNF -7%); KBW called it overdone.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, since it predates the July print by a month. It is filed only because a call comment on lost refi policies could re-surface it.

findings.finding: First American (FAF), the closest peer, reports Q3 2026 after the close on the same evening, 2026-10-21, with its call on 10-22. Its print and order commentary are a same-window read-through for STC. FAF has beaten consensus in 8 of 8 quarters; its Q3 consensus is $1.88.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: FAF beat ($2.08 vs $1.80) and rallied 6.5% the same day STC fell 7.83%, so the read-through did not hold on the last print.
findings.why_not_priced: Its direction is unknown until tonight, so it is sized 0 with a wide band. It adds variance, not sign.

baseline_tension: The negative macro evidence (the rate surge, weak existing-home sales) agrees with the -14.7% 20-day run-up and the 22% drawdown since August, so it is largely priced. There is no usable skew. The light short interest neither adds squeeze risk nor confirms a crowded bear view.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, disputed bar (Benzinga $1.63 vs Tickflow $1.85): capped the rate/guidance finding at -0.8 (was -1.0) and the margin finding at -0.5 (was -0.6).
Rule 6, inside guidance: the Q2 call said no H2 residential growth, so the residential-volume finding went to -0.2 (was -0.3).
Rule 5, a proxy loses to the company's own number: the MSCI -28% commercial proxy went to -0.2 (was -0.4) against STC's own +20%/+30% commercial growth.

Rule 7: short interest was checked before filing the negatives; 3.7% of shares outstanding and 3.2 days to cover is not crowded, so no further shrink. Pessimism artefact: p_up raised from 45 to 46 because the negatives sit on a name already sold 22%.
Left standing: the positioning +0.5, the revenue/MCS +0.3, the title-waiver -0.2 and the FAF read-through at 0.
